problem: Prior hierarchical VLN methods either backtrack heuristically along the recent trajectory (homing) or assume the agent can jump to any visited node (SSM). Neither exploits the topological map to reach promising unvisited nodes, and both encode only spatial-domain visual features that carry little object-level semantics.
motivation: Mistaken actions leave a VLN agent on irrecoverable paths, and generalization to unseen environments suffers. A correction mechanism that picks a promising local goal among unvisited but observable nodes, guided by semantically meaningful object clues, could let the agent recover efficiently without re-exploring visited regions.
key_idea: A learned mode selector switches between exploration and exploitation, and in exploitation the agent plans a path over the topological map to an unvisited candidate local goal chosen by matching category-wise 2D-FFT object features (scene object spectrum, SOS) against reference SOS features built from the instruction's object list.
insight: Local goal search over unvisited candidates using spectral SOS features beats random, homing, and spatial-feature local goal search. On SOON test unseen, spatial-feature search brings no gain over homing (SPL 10.58 vs 19.18), while SOS gives SPL 25.80 and SR 39.09. A language-caption variant (Lang. Aug.) is worse than SOS on R2R. The navigation score correlates linearly with the distance-based nDS in an offline analysis. The gain is largest on unseen splits, suggesting the correction module reduces overfitting.
method: Mode Selector: a two-layer FFN on the cross-modal hidden state H_t gives P_explore = 1 - S_mode(H_t); at or above 0.5 it explores, below 0.5 it exploits. Trained by imitation on ground-truth trajectories augmented with detours.

Cross-modal transformer: pretrained LXMERT-style language encoder with cross-attention and graph-aware self-attention over the topological map (DUET-style), plus location and history encodings; correlation loss L_corr encourages monotonic language-vision alignment.

Exploration module: builds a topological map of visited and unvisited-observable nodes, an FFN exploration policy over candidate nodes (visited nodes masked), and a progress monitor for self-monitoring. Trained with DAgger, then A2C finetuning.

Scene Object Spectrum (SOS): per-category binary masks (unions of detected bounding boxes) on the panorama go through 2D FFT, log magnitude, mean pooling over the vertical axis and normalization, giving a (K, η) feature.

Reference SOS from instruction: object tokens are parsed from the instruction (VQA extracts the target object). Each is approximated by a sinc-shaped spectrum using the median bounding-box width from training data.

Local goal search (exploitation): for each unvisited observed candidate, the shortest-path trajectory from the start node is scored with a pseudo-correlation navigation score S_nav between the reference SOS list and the trajectory's SOS features. The best node becomes the local goal and the agent plans the shortest path to it on the map. This module is not learned; after arrival the mode resets to explore.

setting.backbone: DUET-style topological-map cross-modal transformer (LXMERT language encoder, ViT-B/16 panoramic features) with a mode selector and a non-learned SOS-based exploitation module
setting.training_data: Benchmark training splits (R2R 14,025 episodes, SOON 3,085, REVERIE 10,466), with DUET-style visual encoder pretraining, DAgger, A2C finetuning, and detour-augmented trajectories for the mode selector; pretrained object detectors and VQA are used for parsing
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (ViT-B/16 features) plus detected object bounding boxes/semantic masks; RGBD panoramas in the continuous extensions
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph node selection with shortest-path planning to the local goal (continuous extensions: forward 0.25 m / turn 10° or waypoints)
setting.simulator: Matterport3D simulator (R2R, SOON, REVERIE); Habitat (Gibson image-goal, VLN-CE)
setting.privileged: none (a modified REVERIE object-category dataset with typos fixed and synonyms merged is used for the Meta-Explore* variant)

numbers_note: The REVERIE test-unseen row for the plain Meta-Explore variant is not reported ('-'). Image-goal SR/SPL are printed as fractions (0.84, 0.55) and copied as printed. The R2R baseline table in the paper has some garbled columns for Random and Human rows; these are not used.
results: Meta-Explore reaches R2R test unseen SR 71 / SPL 61 versus DUET 69 / 59. On SOON test unseen it gets SR 39.1 / SPL 25.8 versus DUET 33.4 / 21.4, reported as +17.1% SR and +20.6% SPL. It also beats prior hierarchical methods (SMNA, Regretful-Agent, FAST, SSM). On REVERIE val unseen the gain over DUET is small (SR 47.49 vs 46.98) unless the object categories are cleaned (Meta-Explore* SPL 40.27).
limitations: The exploitation relies on parsing object tokens from instructions and matching them to detector categories, so noisy or synonymous object labels (as in REVERIE) reduce the gain.
No gain on val-seen SOON splits and no FSPL improvement; the continuous-domain SPL on hard image-goal episodes is lower than some graph baselines.
The SOS reference is approximated from median bounding-box widths, which is a coarse proxy for real object appearance.
